options.B: int arr[2][3]; stored row-major in contiguous memory

questions.explanation: C multidimensional arrays are declared as arr[rows][cols] and stored in row-major order contiguously in memory.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Given int arr[5] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}; int *p = arr + 2; what is the value of *(p + 1)?
questions.explanation: arr+2 points to arr[2] (value 30). (p+1) points to arr[3], so dereferencing yields 40.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to arr[i] where arr is an array name?
questions.explanation: In C, array indexing arr[i] is defined as exact syntactic sugar for dereferencing *(arr + i).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the fundamental difference in memory allocation between a struct and a union in C?

options.A: Struct members share memory; union members have separate memory
options.B: Union members share the same memory location; struct members have distinct memory locations
options.C: Structs can hold functions; unions cannot

questions.explanation: A union allocates memory equal to its largest member so all members overlap, whereas struct allocates separate memory for each member.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the potential pitfall of macro definition #define SQUARE(x) x * x when called as SQUARE(2 + 3)?
questions.explanation: SQUARE(2 + 3) expands strictly to 2 + 3 * 2 + 3 = 2 + 6 + 3 = 11. Parentheses around parameters are necessary to fix this.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the difference between malloc(n * sizeof(int)) and calloc(n, sizeof(int))?

options.A: malloc clears memory to 0; calloc leaves uninitialized garbage
options.B: calloc clears allocated memory to zero; malloc leaves memory contents uninitialized
options.C: malloc is used for structs; calloc for primitives

questions.explanation: calloc initializes allocated heap bytes to zero, whereas malloc leaves memory unitialized.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which C file function is used to write formatted output directly to a file stream?
questions.explanation: fprintf() works like printf() but outputs formatted text to a specified FILE pointer stream.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort algorithm?
questions.explanation: Quick sort degrades to O(N^2) worst-case time when pivot selection is poor (e.g. already sorted array with end pivot).

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Linked lists and basic data structures
questions.question: In a singly linked list node structure struct Node { int data; struct Node *next; }; what does 'next' store?

options.B: The memory address of the next Node

questions.explanation: The 'next' member is a self-referential pointer storing the memory address of the subsequent list node.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is integer promotion in C expression evaluation?

options.B: Automatic conversion of integer types smaller than int (like char or short) to int/unsigned int during expressions

questions.explanation: C automatically promotes small integer types (char, short) to int or unsigned int before evaluating expressions.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Given int matrix[2][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}}; what is the value of matrix[1][2]?
questions.explanation: matrix[1] accesses the second row {4, 5, 6}, and matrix[1][2] accesses the 3rd element in that row, which is 6.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which standard function safely copies a string up to n characters preventing buffer overflow?
questions.explanation: strncpy() copies at most n characters from source to destination buffer.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What does the 'extern' keyword signify in variable declarations?

options.A: Variable is stored in external disk
options.B: Variable is declared here but defined in another translation unit/file

questions.explanation: 'extern' specifies that a variable/function has external linkage and is defined in another file or scope.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the effect of expression x ^ x for any integer variable x?
questions.explanation: XORing any number with itself results in 0 because matching bits cancel out (1^1=0, 0^0=0).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the output of the stringification operator '#' in macro #define STR(x) #x?

options.A: Converts macro argument x into a string literal "x"

questions.explanation: The single '#' operator converts the macro parameter into a quoted string literal.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What happens if realloc(ptr, new_size) cannot expand memory in place and allocates a new memory block?

options.B: Copies old contents to new location, frees old block, and returns new pointer

questions.explanation: realloc copies existing data to the newly allocated block, frees the old block memory automatically, and returns the new address.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What does the fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END) call do in C file handling?

options.B: Positions file position indicator to the end of the file stream

questions.explanation: fseek with SEEK_END sets the file position indicator to the file end, useful for determining file size via ftell().

questions.subject: C
questions.question: For command `./app input.txt 100`, what is argv[1]?
questions.explanation: argv[0] is executable name ("./app"), and argv[1] is the first argument string ("input.txt").

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What precondition must be met before executing Binary Search on an array?

options.A: Array elements must be floating point
options.B: Array must be sorted in order

questions.explanation: Binary search requires a pre-sorted array to eliminate half of the remaining elements at each step.

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Linked lists and basic data structures
questions.question: What is the time complexity of pushing an item onto a stack implemented with a linked list?
questions.explanation: Inserting at the head of a linked list stack takes constant O(1) time.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What compiler warning or error occurs if a non-void function reaches the end without a return statement?

options.A: Control reaches end of non-void function

questions.explanation: Compilers issue a warning 'control reaches end of non-void function' because returning without a value causes undefined behavior when caller uses return value.

questions.question: If int *p = (int*)1000; on a system where sizeof(int) == 4, what is the value of p + 2?
questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic scales increments by sizeof(*p). 1000 + 2 * 4 = 1008.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is typedef used for when defining a struct in C?

options.A: To create an alias name for the struct type avoiding mandatory 'struct' keyword in declarations

questions.explanation: typedef creates a custom type alias (e.g. typedef struct Node Node;) so you can write 'Node n;' instead of 'struct Node n;'.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: How can you check if an integer x is odd using bitwise operators?
questions.explanation: An integer is odd if its least significant bit (LSB) is 1. Bitwise AND with 1 tests the LSB.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is printed by printf("%c", *("Programming" + 3));?
questions.explanation: "Programming" is char pointer to 'P' (index 0). Index + 3 points to 'g' (P=0, r=1, o=2, g=3).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: How can a C function modify a caller variable's value?

options.B: By passing pointer address of variable as argument
options.D: C functions cannot modify caller variables

questions.explanation: Passing a variable's memory address (pointer) allows the function to dereference and modify the caller's memory value.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What issue is caused by calling free(ptr); twice on the same allocated pointer?
questions.explanation: Freeing the same pointer twice corrupts memory allocator internal structures resulting in undefined behavior or crash.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the space complexity of an in-place Selection Sort algorithm?
questions.explanation: In-place selection sort requires O(1) auxiliary memory space beyond the input array.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has a stable best, average, and worst-case time complexity of O(N log N)?
questions.explanation: Merge sort recursively divides array and merges, maintaining O(N log N) across all cases.

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Undefined behavior and common programming errors
questions.question: What is a dangling pointer in C?

options.B: Pointer pointing to memory that has been deallocated/freed

questions.explanation: A dangling pointer holds the address of a memory block that has already been deallocated or freed.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the purpose of the valgrind tool in C development?

options.B: Detecting memory leaks and invalid memory accesses

questions.explanation: Valgrind is a dynamic analysis tool used to detect memory leaks, uninitialized memory reads, and buffer overrides.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What happens if a switch case block lacks a 'break' statement?

options.B: Fall-through to subsequent case blocks until break or end is reached

questions.explanation: Lacking a break statement causes execution to fall through into subsequent switch case blocks.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the return value of strcmp("apple", "banana")?
questions.explanation: strcmp compares strings lexicographically. 'apple' precedes 'banana' in ASCII, returning a value less than 0.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the size in bytes of array double arr[10] on a platform where sizeof(double) == 8?
questions.explanation: Total array memory size is element count multiplied by sizeof(type): 10 * 8 = 80 bytes.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which macro conditional directive checks if a macro identifier is NOT defined?
questions.explanation: #ifndef (if not defined) checks whether a macro name has not been defined previously.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Can C functions return a structure by value?

options.A: No, C functions can only return primitive types
options.B: Yes, C supports returning structures by value
options.C: Only if struct size is under 8 bytes

questions.explanation: C fully supports returning entire struct instances by value from functions.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the output of printf("%d", sizeof(void*)) on a 64-bit platform?
questions.explanation: On a 64-bit architecture system, all object pointers (including void*) are 8 bytes (64 bits) wide.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which standard file open mode opens a binary file for appending data?
questions.explanation: "ab" opens a file in binary mode for appending at end of file.

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Linked lists and basic data structures
questions.question: Which data structure operates on a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order?
questions.explanation: A Stack data structure stores and retrieves elements in Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which stage of C compilation expands macros and handles #include directives?
questions.explanation: The Preprocessor stage processes #include, #define macros, and conditional compilation directives before compilation.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the main task of the Linker in C build pipeline?

options.B: Combining compiled object files (.o/.obj) and library code into a single executable file

questions.explanation: The Linker resolves external symbols and combines object files into a single binary executable file.

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Undefined behavior and common programming errors
questions.question: What type of error is caused by dividing an integer variable by zero at runtime in C?
questions.explanation: Division by zero is undefined behavior in C standard, typically triggering a runtime exception/signal.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the result of expression ~0 in 32-bit two's complement integer arithmetic?
questions.explanation: Bitwise NOT (~0) flips all 32 zero bits to ones (0xFFFFFFFF), representing -1 in two's complement format.
